anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet the 24-pin FPC connector J9 (FH34SRJ-24S-0.5SH(99)) carries no-connect (X) flags on pins 1-8, including pin 2 and pin 3. Consequently the boost MOSFET Q2 (MCH3478-TL-W) gate (pin 1) and the current-sense resistor R3 (0.47 ohm) / Q2 source return terminate at no-connect pins rather than into the panel. The display control signals on J9 pins 9-14 (NET0053/NET0008/NET0035/NET0006/NET0044/NET0016) are wired normally, so the connector is not mirror-numbered.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification, J1.2 (GDR) must drive the boost MOSFET gate and J1.3 (RESE) must connect the MOSFET source / R1 sense node back to the panel, closing the boost-converter control loop entirely within the EPD module and external power stage. The spec states: "Q1's gate ... is driven from J1.2 ... Q1's source ... returns through R1 (0.47 ohm) to GND and also feeds back to J1.3 (RESE)".

evidence.quote: EPD_Driver.kicad_sch: J9 pins 1-8 drawn with no-connect (X) markers; Q2 (MCH3478-TL-W) gate and R3 (0.47ohm) sense node end at those no-connect pins.

Boost converter operation: Q1's gate (Net-(Q1-G)) is driven from J1.2 ... Q1's source (Net-(Q1-S)) returns through R1 (0.47 ohm) to GND and also feeds back to J1.3 (RESE) ... closing the control loop entirely within the EPD module and external power stage.

anomalies.impact: With GDR and RESE left open, the e-paper panel's COG driver cannot generate the boost switching signal nor sense the inductor current, so Q2 never switches and the high-voltage rails (VGH/VGL/VCOM) required to drive the Waveshare 2.13" panel are never produced. The display will not refresh / will not power up, even though the SPI command lines and the Q3 power-switch are intact.

parsed.summary: The schematic is a functionally faithful but globally renumbered copy of the reference (every reference designator is shifted, which is not a behavioural deviation), but on the EPD_Driver sheet the FPC connector's GDR (pin 2) and RESE (pin 3) are drawn as no-connect, leaving the boost MOSFET gate and current-sense feedback floating; this breaks the EPD boost-converter control loop and would prevent the e-paper display from ever generating its high-voltage rails.
